precepts.text: Men of low degree are vanity and men of high degree are a lie; laid in the balance they are altogether lighter than vanity, so the life we have is vain and short-lived.
precepts.point: When you die you take no wisdom and no riches with you. A man heaps up riches and does not even know who shall gather them.

note.label: Psalm 39: David Mourns His Frailty and Prays to Recover Strength

precepts.why:
“verily every man at his best state is altogether vanity.” Psalm 62 says it of every rank of man: “Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.” So the life we have is vain and short-lived. At your prime you are nothing; you cannot measure up to the Most High.

David asks the Lord to make him know his end and the measure of his days, that he may know how frail he is; this is him going through his affliction and thinking on his own death. Men's lives are short, and the sentence for all flesh is death. When you die you take no wisdom and no riches with you: a man “heapeth up riches, and knoweth not who shall gather them.”

Look at how the Most High cut down our days, from the hundreds of years he originally gave to 120, then to 70. You rarely see people pass 100 years. “thou hast made my days as an handbreadth; and mine age is as nothing before thee”.

precepts.text: The Lord gave the word; the forefathers wrote down what the Lord said through them.
precepts.point: They came round about him daily like water, dogs have compassed him, like it says in Psalm 22; lover and friend are put far from him and his acquaintance into darkness. These are the prophecies of our forefathers, and this is the real black history, the Most High declaring the end from the beginning to strengthen our faith.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
Everything in Psalm 88, the soul cast off, the face hidden, the terrors, the dogs compassing him about, was written before it happened to Christ. How? “God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto God.”

The Lord gave the word; the forefathers wrote down what the Lord said through them. Power belongs unto God, and that includes the power to declare the end from the beginning. That is why these prophecies are the real black history, given to strengthen our faith: what our forefathers wrote was heard from the Most High.

points: Truly David's soul waits upon God, from whom comes his salvation; He only is his rock and salvation and defense, so he shall not be greatly moved.

note.label: Psalm 62: Let Your Expectation Be of God

points: He rebukes those who imagine mischief against a man, who shall be slain like a bowing wall and a tottering fence; they consult to cast him down from his excellency, delight in lies, and bless with their mouth but curse inwardly.

note.label: Psalm 62: Let Your Expectation Be of God

points: David tells his own soul to wait only upon God, for his expectation is from Him; He only is his rock, salvation, defense, glory, and refuge.

note.label: Psalm 62: Let Your Expectation Be of God

points: A lot of us expect things from men and expect people not to let us down. "I expected more of you," "I expected you to be this way," and that is your problem. Let your expectations be of God, as David's expectations were of God. You cannot change anybody, but God can.
Trust in Him at all times, pour out your heart before Him, for God is a refuge for us.

note.label: Psalm 62: Let Your Expectation Be of God

points: Men of low degree are vanity and men of high degree are a lie; laid in the balance they are altogether lighter than vanity. Trust not in oppression, become not vain in robbery, and if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.

note.label: Psalm 62: Let Your Expectation Be of God

points: God has spoken once, twice have we heard this: that power belongs to God, and to Him belongs mercy, for He renders to every man according to his work.
